countries.name: Uganda
countries.summary: Uganda is an East African nation home to Mbarara University of Science and Technology, a public university whose Faculty of Medicine runs a WHO-listed, direct-entry Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (MBChB) programme with a distinctive community-based education model.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: Uganda offers an internationally recognized, WHO-listed medical degree taught entirely in English, a direct-entry five-year curriculum with early community health exposure, and tuition markedly lower than most other MBBS-abroad destinations.
countries.climate: Tropical climate with generally mild temperatures year-round due to elevation, and two rainy seasons.

universities.name: Mbarara University of Science and Technology Faculty of Medicine
universities.summary: Mbarara University of Science and Technology (MUST) Faculty of Medicine runs a direct-entry, five-year, English-medium Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (MBChB) programme built around a distinctive community-based education model. The university is listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools with ECFMG-certification eligibility, and is on the Uganda Medical and Dental Practitioners Council's official list of approved medical schools.
universities.campusLifestyle: International students join the MBChB cohort across MUST's Kihumuro Main Campus and City Campus in Mbarara, with an International Relations Office supporting pre-arrival guidance, visa/student-pass steps and accommodation options.
universities.cityProfile: Mbarara is a regional city in southwestern Uganda, home to MUST's campuses and a growing international-student community, with typical off-campus rents notably lower than East Africa's larger capital cities.
universities.practicalExposure: The five-year MBChB programme runs preclinical basic sciences in Years 1-2 (anatomy, histology, physiology, biochemistry, microbiology, pharmacology), transitions through pathology and clinical-methods modules, and moves into full clinical training in Years 4-5 (emergency medicine, surgery, family medicine, psychiatry, and specialty rotations), integrated throughout with MUST's Community Based Education, Research and Services (COBERS) model, in which students engage directly in interdisciplinary community healthcare delivery as part of the standard curriculum.
universities.hostelOverview: On-campus residence accommodation is available at both MUST campuses on a first-come, first-served basis, though no specific rate is published; short-stay Expatriate Quarters are available at USD 5/night for occasional or elective visitors. Typical off-campus rents in Mbarara range from roughly USD 82-125/month for a 1-bedroom apartment to USD 191-246/month for a 2-bedroom apartment in the city centre, per the university's own International Office cost guide.
universities.dietarySupport: An average campus meal costs roughly USD 1-2 per the university's own cost-of-living guide; no separate university-run meal-plan cost is published.
universities.safetyOverview: No university-published campus-safety statistics were found during research.
universities.studentSupport: International applicants apply through MUST's own online portal, pay application fees via international wire transfer to a Uganda Revenue Authority account, and are supported by a dedicated International Relations Office with a published pre-arrival guide.
whyChoose: Listed in the WHO World Directory of Medical Schools (FAIMER School ID F0000068), with graduates (1989-current) eligible to apply for ECFMG Certification and no entrance exam required for the standard direct-entry route.
On the Uganda Medical and Dental Practitioners Council's own official list of approved East African medical schools.
A distinctive Community Based Education, Research and Services (COBERS) model giving students early, structured community-health exposure throughout the curriculum.
A published, dual (domestic/international) fee schedule directly on the official programme page, with international tuition markedly lower than most other MBBS-abroad destinations.
A confirmed live, active 2026/27 admissions cycle, evidenced by dated admission-list updates through mid-2026.
thingsToConsider: The published international tuition figure (roughly USD 1,700-1,750/year at recent exchange rates) is notably lower than typical MBBS-abroad international pricing elsewhere; confirm this figure directly with MUST admissions before committing, since no separate international-fee-schedule document exists to cross-verify it.

MUST's official 2026/27 admissions announcement confirms an August 2026 intake but does not publish an exact day-level application deadline in machine-readable form; confirm the precise deadline directly with the university.

The specific international application fee amount could not be confirmed from an official MUST document during research; only the payment mechanism (international wire transfer to a Uganda Revenue Authority account) is confirmed.
No MBChB-specific international scholarship is published; MUST's only listed scholarship (OWSD WISDOM) is a postgraduate, women-only award unrelated to this programme.
No specific affiliated teaching hospital name was found on MUST's own official pages during this research pass; confirm current clinical-training sites directly with the university.

faq.question: Is the MBChB programme direct-entry after high school?
faq.answer: Yes. Direct entry requires two principal passes in Biology and Chemistry plus at least a subsidiary pass in Physics or Mathematics at the secondary-school (A-Level or equivalent) stage; no prior university degree is required, and no entrance exam applies to this standard route.

faq.question: What qualification is awarded on graduation?
faq.answer: Graduates receive the Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBChB) degree after five years of study.

faq.question: How are foreign secondary-school qualifications evaluated?
faq.answer: Foreign qualifications equivalent to Uganda's UCE/UACE certificates are equated through the Uganda National Examinations Board (UNEB); no Indian-curriculum-specific conversion table is published, so applicants should confirm the equating process directly with the university.

faq.question: What is the current tuition fee?
faq.answer: The official programme page publishes a dual fee schedule: international students pay double the domestic rate, working out to roughly USD 1,700-1,750/year combined tuition and functional fees at recent exchange rates -- notably lower than many other MBBS-abroad destinations, so confirm this figure directly with MUST admissions before committing.

faq.question: Is there a written entrance exam?
faq.answer: No. The WHO World Directory of Medical Schools confirms no entrance exam is required for the standard direct-entry MBChB route (a separate entrance exam applies only to the university's alternative Diploma-Entry pathway).

faq.question: When does the academic year start and when can I apply?
faq.answer: The intake is in August. MUST's official 2026/27 admissions announcement confirms this cycle is active, though an exact day-level application deadline could not be confirmed from the available official documents -- confirm directly with the university.

faq.question: Is university accommodation available?
faq.answer: On-campus residence accommodation is available at both MUST campuses on a first-come, first-served basis, though no specific rate is published; short-stay Expatriate Quarters are available at USD 5/night. Off-campus 1-bedroom apartments in Mbarara typically run USD 82-125/month.

faq.question: Do Indian students need NEET to join this programme?
faq.answer: The university's own admissions criteria do not reference NEET. Separately, India's National Medical Commission requires Indian citizens who obtain a primary medical qualification abroad to have qualified NEET-UG and, on return, to clear its Foreign Medical Graduate licensure pathway; this general framework was not independently verified against an NMC source for this specific programme.

programmes.officialTitle: Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBChB)

fee.notes: Officially published international-student rate: UGX 2,688,000/semester tuition (2 semesters/year = UGX 5,376,000/year), double the Ugandan domestic rate, plus a separate UGX 1,100,000/year functional fee (also double the domestic rate). Combined this is roughly USD 1,700-1,750/year at recent exchange rates -- notably lower than typical MBBS-abroad international pricing, which is unusual enough that it should be reconfirmed directly with MUST admissions before being treated as final, since no separate cross-verifying international-fee-schedule document was found. Total is calculated as the annual tuition figure times 5 years -- not published as a lump sum, and excludes the functional fee and other charges.

eligibleAudiences: International applicants who have completed secondary education with two principal passes in Biology and Chemistry plus a subsidiary pass in Physics or Mathematics
restrictions: Foreign secondary qualifications must be equated by the Uganda National Examinations Board (UNEB) before admission
Applicants whose medium of instruction was not English must provide recognized evidence of English proficiency
audienceEligibility.notes: No entrance exam applies to the standard direct-entry route; an entrance exam applies only to the university's separate Diploma-Entry pathway.

admissionsContent.overview: International applicants register on MUST's own online admissions portal, untick the 'I sat for UNEB' option, submit and pay for their application form, then pay the application fee via international wire transfer to a Uganda Revenue Authority account before emailing proof of payment to the admissions office.

eligibility.intro: Admission requires completed secondary education meeting the minimum science-subject grades, with foreign qualifications equated by UNEB.
items: Two principal passes in Biology and Chemistry, plus at least a subsidiary pass in Physics or Mathematics
UNEB equating certificate for foreign secondary-school qualifications
Recognized evidence of English proficiency if prior schooling was not English-medium

applicationSteps: Register on MUST's online application portal (applications.must.ac.ug)
Complete the application form, unticking the 'I sat for UNEB' option as a non-Ugandan applicant
Upload required documents and generate a payment reference number
Pay the application fee via international wire transfer to MUST's Uganda Revenue Authority account
Email proof of payment to the admissions office and await a decision
